    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_skips_inactive_authorities() {
        // The authorities are born Registered and never activated: nothing is
        // Active, so a broadcast delivers to nobody — inactive authorities
        // never receive platform messages.
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast, HubId::WORKSPACE, None);
        let receipt = backbone.broadcast(message).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn messages_carry_a_domain_neutral_payload() {
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Notification,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        )
        .with_payload(BackbonePayload::None);
        assert_eq!(message.payload(), BackbonePayload::None);
        // The plain constructor also carries the empty payload.
        let plain = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Notification, HubId::DEVICE, None);
        assert_eq!(plain.payload(), BackbonePayload::None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_delivers_a_log_request_to_the_log_service() {
        // Phase 7F.1 proof chain: Backbone → LogAuthority → LogService →
        // ServiceResult.
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        // 1. The backbone delivers the proof request to the Log Authority
        //    (cloned: the message is read again below for the invocation).
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let receipt = backbone.dispatch(message.clone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::LOG));
        // 2. The Log Authority forwards it to its owned service, which
        //    returns its ServiceResult.
        let authority = kernel
            .authorities()
            .iter()
            .find(|authority| authority.id() == HubId::LOG)
            .expect("the ready kernel owns the log authority");
        let invocation = crate::hub::service::ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(
            authority.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(),
            crate::hub::service::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_delivers_a_domain_request_to_its_service() {
        // Phase 7F.2 chain: Backbone → WorkspaceAuthority → WorkspaceService
        // → ServiceResult, carrying the minimal service-operation payload.
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(BackbonePayload::Operation(ServiceOperation::Accept));
        // 1. The backbone delivers the request to the Workspace Authority
        //    (cloned: the message is read again below for the invocation).
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let receipt = backbone.dispatch(message.clone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::WORKSPACE));
        // 2. The Workspace Authority forwards it to its owned service.
        let authority = kernel
            .authorities()
            .iter()
            .find(|authority| authority.id() == HubId::WORKSPACE)
            .expect("the ready kernel owns the workspace authority");
        let invocation = crate::hub::service::ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(
            authority.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(),
            crate::hub::service::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_delivers_real_operations_to_the_workspace_domain() {
        // Phase 7F.3 chain: Backbone → WorkspaceAuthority → WorkspaceService
        // → domain state → ServiceResult / Response, carrying the real
        // domain operation payload.
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let open = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(BackbonePayload::Operation(ServiceOperation::Open(
            "ra-main".to_owned(),
        )));
        // 1. The backbone delivers the open operation to the Workspace
        //    Authority (cloned: the message is read again below).
        let receipt = backbone.dispatch(open.clone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::WORKSPACE));
        // 2. The Workspace Authority forwards it to its owned service, which
        //    performs the real domain operation.
        let authority = kernel
            .authorities()
            .iter()
            .find(|authority| authority.id() == HubId::WORKSPACE)
            .expect("the ready kernel owns the workspace authority");
        let open_invocation = crate::hub::service::ServiceInvocation::new(&open);
        assert_eq!(
            authority.invoke(&open_invocation).unwrap(),
            crate::hub::service::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // 3. A question is answered with the real domain state — the
        //    synchronous Response path.
        let inspect = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(BackbonePayload::Operation(ServiceOperation::Inspect));
        let inspect_invocation = crate::hub::service::ServiceInvocation::new(&inspect);
        assert_eq!(
            authority.invoke(&inspect_invocation).unwrap(),
            crate::hub::service::ServiceResult::Inspected("workspace: ra-main".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn correlation_sequences_are_sequential_and_deterministic() {
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let first = sequence.next();
        let second = sequence.next();
        assert_ne!(first, second, "correlation ids must be distinct");
        assert_eq!(first.to_string(), "1");
        assert_eq!(second.to_string(), "2");
    }

    #[test]
    fn messages_carry_an_optional_correlation_identifier() {
        // Every Phase 7E–7F.3 envelope carries no correlation; the round-trip
        // attaches one through `with_correlation`.
        let plain = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Request, HubId::DEVICE, None);
        assert_eq!(plain.correlation(), None);
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let correlation = sequence.next();
        let request = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_correlation(correlation)
        .with_payload(BackbonePayload::Operation(ServiceOperation::Inspect));
        assert_eq!(request.correlation(), Some(correlation));
    }

    #[test]
    fn service_results_map_explicitly_to_response_payloads() {
        // The explicit ServiceResult → Response conversion boundary: every
        // service outcome maps to exactly one response payload.
        assert_eq!(
            ResponsePayload::from_service_result(ServiceResult::Accepted),
            ResponsePayload::Accepted
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ResponsePayload::from_service_result(ServiceResult::Completed),
            ResponsePayload::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ResponsePayload::from_service_result(ServiceResult::Rejected),
            ResponsePayload::Rejected
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ResponsePayload::from_service_result(ServiceResult::Inspected("x".to_owned())),
            ResponsePayload::Inspected("x".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_response_is_a_correlated_response_message() {
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let correlation = sequence.next();
        let response = Response::new(
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(correlation),
            ResponsePayload::Inspected("workspace: none".to_owned()),
        );
        assert_eq!(response.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Response);
        assert_eq!(response.source(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(response.target(), Some(HubId::DEVICE));
        assert_eq!(response.correlation(), Some(correlation));
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &ResponsePayload::Inspected("workspace: none".to_owned())
        );
        // The Response message itself carries the response payload.
        assert_eq!(
            response.message().payload(),
            BackbonePayload::Response(ResponsePayload::Inspected("workspace: none".to_owned()))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_response_answers_the_request_it_correlates_with() {
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let request = sequence.next();
        let other = sequence.next();
        let response = Response::new(
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(request),
            ResponsePayload::Completed,
        );
        assert!(response.answers(request));
        assert!(
            !response.answers(other),
            "a response never answers an unrelated request"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn verify_answers_rejects_a_mismatched_or_missing_correlation() {
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let request = sequence.next();
        let other = sequence.next();
        let response = Response::new(
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(request),
            ResponsePayload::Completed,
        );
        assert!(response.verify_answers(request).is_ok());
        // A mismatched correlation is rejected.
        assert_eq!(
            response.verify_answers(other),
            Err(HubError::CorrelationMismatch {
                expected: other,
                actual: Some(request),
            })
        );
        // A missing correlation identifier is rejected.
        let missing = Response::new(
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            None,
            ResponsePayload::Completed,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            missing.verify_answers(request),
            Err(HubError::CorrelationMismatch {
                expected: request,
                actual: None,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_request_cannot_be_broadcast() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        // A request always addresses a hub; it cannot travel as a broadcast.
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Request, HubId::LOG, None);
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.broadcast(message),
            Err(HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
                kind: BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                operation: "broadcast",
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_response_cannot_be_broadcast() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        // A response always addresses the requesting caller; it cannot travel
        // as a broadcast.
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Response, HubId::LOG, None);
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.broadcast(message),
            Err(HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
                kind: BackboneMessageKind::Response,
                operation: "broadcast",
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_requires_a_concrete_target_for_requests() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        // A request always addresses a hub: a target-less request is
        // rejected.
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Request, HubId::DEVICE, None);
        assert_eq!(backbone.dispatch(message), Err(HubError::TargetRequired));
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_rejects_an_unregistered_request_target() {
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::UnregisteredTarget(HubId::LOG))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_rejects_an_inactive_request_target() {
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::STORAGE),
        );
        // Storage is registered but its authority is still Registered: only
        // Active hubs are dispatched to.
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::STORAGE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reply_delivers_a_correlated_response_back_to_the_caller() {
        // Phase 7F.4: a Response echoing the Request's correlation is
        // delivered back over the backbone to the requesting caller.
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let correlation = sequence.next();
        let response = Response::new(
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(correlation),
            ResponsePayload::Inspected("workspace: none".to_owned()),
        );
        let receipt = backbone.reply(response.message().clone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Response);
        assert_eq!(receipt.source(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::DEVICE));
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_rejects_normal_traffic_while_the_platform_is_suspended() {
        // Phase 7F.5: suspension moves every authority out of Active; the
        // backbone lifecycle gate (the existing per-authority Active gate)
        // then rejects normal service requests instead of fabricating a
        // successful delivery receipt.
        let mut kernel = ready_kernel();
        kernel.suspend().unwrap();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::WORKSPACE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_rejects_normal_traffic_after_shutdown() {
        // Phase 7F.5: shutdown terminates every authority; normal requests
        // are rejected permanently — no new traffic enters the platform.
        let mut kernel = ready_kernel();
        kernel.shutdown().unwrap();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::LOG))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_reaches_no_authority_while_suspended() {
        // Phase 7F.5: a platform-wide broadcast is delivered to every Active
        // authority — while the platform is suspended none is Active, so the
        // receipt records zero recipients and no domain operation executes.
        let mut kernel = ready_kernel();
        kernel.suspend().unwrap();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast, HubId::DEVICE, None);
        let receipt = backbone.broadcast(message).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 0);
    }
}

=== AUTHORITY ===
//! Hub authorities (Phase 7D.2).
//!
//! The **hub authority** is the concrete, per-domain ownership object of the
//! Platform Kernel. Phase 7D.1 defined the hub **contracts** — the static
//! [`Hub`] metadata, the [`HubDomain`] vocabulary, the stable [`HubId`]s and
//! the [`HubLifecycle`] states. Phase 7D.2 turns those contracts into the
//! eight concrete authorities the kernel will run on:
//!
//! * [`WorkspaceAuthority`] — owns the workspace domain;
//! * [`ProjectAuthority`] — owns the project domain;
//! * [`PackageAuthority`] — owns the package domain;
//! * [`SettingsAuthority`] — owns the settings domain;
//! * [`HistoryAuthority`] — owns the history domain;
//! * [`LogAuthority`] — owns the log domain;
//! * [`StorageAuthority`] — owns the storage domain;
//! * [`DeviceAuthority`] — owns the device domain.
//!
//! Every authority:
//!
//! * owns **exactly one platform domain** (its type fixes its domain — a
//!   [`WorkspaceAuthority`] can never own anything but the workspace domain);
//! * **composes the hub metadata** ([`Hub`]) — the static id/domain pair the
//!   authority is the owner of;
//! * **exposes its lifecycle state** ([`HubLifecycle`]);
//! * **acknowledges backbone delivery** through a controlled delivery
//!   boundary ([`HubAuthority::receive`]) — the only way a message reaches an
//!   authority (Phase 7E.1);
//! * **owns its services** — reached through a controlled service boundary
//!   ([`HubAuthority::service`], [`HubAuthority::invoke`]): every authority
//!   owns the service of its domain, and invocation forwards platform
//!   requests to the owned service (Phases 7F.1–7F.2);
//! * **supports registration** with the hub [`Registry`] (delegated from the
//!   authority; the registration *orchestration* is Phase 7D.3);
//! * exposes **no domain operations** (no save, load, compile or run);
//! * contains **no business logic**.
//!
//! # Lifecycle state placement
//!
//! Phase 7D.1 left the placement of per-hub lifecycle state open. Phase 7D.2
//! decides: the lifecycle state lives **on the authority** (this module), not
//! on the static [`Hub`] metadata. Authorities are born
//! [`HubLifecycle::Registered`] — the first state of the documented chain
//! (`Registered → Initialized → Active ⇄ Suspended → Shutdown`).
//!
//! Phase 7D.3 implements the **startup transitions**; Phase 7F.5 completes
//! the lifecycle:
//!
//! * [`HubAuthority::initialize`] — `Registered → Initialized`;
//! * [`HubAuthority::activate`] — `Initialized → Active`;
//! * [`HubAuthority::suspend`] — `Active → Suspended`;
//! * [`HubAuthority::resume`] — `Suspended → Active`;
//! * [`HubAuthority::shutdown`] — `Active | Suspended → Shutdown`.
//!
//! Every named transition delegates to the **single validated transition
//! mechanism** ([`HubAuthority::transition`]), which applies the one
//! transition table ([`HubLifecycle::can_transition`]); transition logic is
//! never duplicated across authorities. Suspension **preserves** domain
//! state (pause, not shutdown); shutdown is terminal. The aggregate
//! platform control lives on the Platform Kernel (the `kernel` module), the
//! owner of aggregate lifecycle control.
//!
//! # Authority ownership
//!
//! The ownership chain of each platform domain is fixed:
//!
//! `Authority → State → Services → Events → Policies`
//!
//! The authority owns exactly one domain and owns that domain's **state**,
//! **services**, **events** and **policies**. **Services never own
//! authorities** — an authority owns its services, never the other way
//! around. The Platform Backbone (the `backbone` module) dispatches to
//! authorities; services are reached through their owning authority, never
//! directly.
//!
//! # Scope
//!
//! Phase 7E.1: authorities are ownership objects with one addition — the
//! controlled backbone **delivery boundary** ([`HubAuthority::receive`]),
//! which acknowledges receipt without doing any work. Phase 7F.1 adds the
//! controlled **service boundary** ([`HubAuthority::service`],
//! [`HubAuthority::invoke`]). Phase 7F.2 binds every authority to the
//! service of its domain. Phase 7F.3: the services behind the boundary own
//! real domain state and perform real domain operations — the authority
//! remains the domain owner and forwards requests to its owned service, and
//! the frozen kernel ownership is untouched.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use super::backbone::{BackboneMessage, DeliveryReceipt};
use super::service::{
    DeviceService, HistoryService, LogService, PackageService, ProjectService, Service,
    ServiceInvocation, ServiceResult, SettingsService, StorageService, WorkspaceService,
};
use super::{Hub, HubDomain, HubError, HubId, HubLifecycle, HubResult, Registry};

/// The authoritative ownership contract of a single platform domain.
///
/// Implemented by every concrete hub authority. The trait exposes the
/// authority's identity, its composed hub metadata and its lifecycle state —
/// nothing more. It deliberately exposes **no domain operations**.
pub(crate) trait HubAuthority {
    /// Returns the stable identifier of this authority in the hub graph.
    fn id(&self) -> HubId;

    /// Returns the platform domain this authority owns.
    fn domain(&self) -> HubDomain;

    /// Returns the composed hub metadata (the static id/domain pair).
    fn hub(&self) -> &Hub;

    /// Returns the current lifecycle state of this authority.
    fn lifecycle(&self) -> HubLifecycle;

    /// Sets the authority's lifecycle state.
    ///
    /// Storage primitive backing the validated default transitions
    /// ([`HubAuthority::transition`]); concrete authorities implement it by
    /// writing their own lifecycle field. **Not** a transition by itself —
    /// callers must go through the validated transition mechanism.
    fn set_lifecycle(&mut self, lifecycle: HubLifecycle);

    /// The single validated lifecycle transition mechanism (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// Validates `self`'s current state against `to` using the one
    /// transition table ([`HubLifecycle::can_transition`]) and applies the
    /// transition when it is allowed. Fails with
    /// [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] otherwise. Every named transition
    /// (`initialize`, `activate`, `suspend`, `resume`, `shutdown`)
    /// delegates here — transition logic is never duplicated across
    /// authorities.
    fn transition(&mut self, to: HubLifecycle) -> HubResult<()> {
        let from = self.lifecycle();
        if !from.can_transition(to) {
            return Err(HubError::InvalidTransition { from, to });
        }
        self.set_lifecycle(to);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Startup transition: `Registered → Initialized`.
    ///
    /// Fails with [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] when the authority is not
    /// in the [`HubLifecycle::Registered`] state.
    fn initialize(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.transition(HubLifecycle::Initialized)
    }

    /// Startup transition: `Initialized → Active`.
    ///
    /// Fails with [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] when the authority is not
    /// in the [`HubLifecycle::Initialized`] state.
    fn activate(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.transition(HubLifecycle::Active)
    }

    /// Suspension transition: `Active → Suspended` (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// A suspended authority is **paused, not shut down**: it is never
    /// routed to, its services are unavailable for normal execution, and its
    /// domain state is preserved for a later [`HubAuthority::resume`]. Fails
    /// with [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] when the authority is not
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Active`].
    fn suspend(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.transition(HubLifecycle::Suspended)
    }

    /// Resume transition: `Suspended → Active` (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// Restores an authority suspended by [`HubAuthority::suspend`]; the
    /// domain state preserved during suspension remains available and the
    /// authority is routed to again. Fails with
    /// [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] when the authority is not
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Suspended`].
    fn resume(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.transition(HubLifecycle::Active)
    }

    /// Shutdown transition: `Active | Suspended → Shutdown` (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// Terminates the authority: it is never routed to again and its
    /// services can never execute again. [`HubLifecycle::Shutdown`] is
    /// terminal — no transition out of it exists. Fails with
    /// [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] when the authority is neither
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Active`] nor [`HubLifecycle::Suspended`].
    fn shutdown(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.transition(HubLifecycle::Shutdown)
    }

    /// Registers this authority with `registry` under its hub id.
    ///
    /// Delegates to [`Registry::register`] with the authority's composed hub
    /// metadata; fails with
    /// [`crate::hub::HubError::AlreadyRegistered`] when the id is taken.
    /// This is the per-authority registration capability only — registering
    /// the full set of authorities and activating them is the Phase 7D.3
    /// orchestration.
    fn register(&self, registry: &mut Registry) -> HubResult<()> {
        registry.register(*self.hub())
    }

    /// The controlled backbone **delivery boundary**.
    ///
    /// Called **only** by the Platform Backbone (the `backbone` module) when
    /// a message is delivered to this authority; the authority acknowledges
    /// receipt with a [`DeliveryReceipt`] that **is** the delivery result the
    /// backbone returns. The backbone is the single communication path of the
    /// platform — callers must never bypass it.
    ///
    /// The returned receipt describes this single authority's acknowledgment
    /// (recipients `1`); a platform-wide broadcast aggregates the per-authority
    /// acknowledgments into one receipt on the backbone side.
    ///
    /// Phase 7E.1: the default acknowledgment performs no work and exposes no
    /// internal state. Service invocation happens through the controlled
    /// invocation boundary ([`HubAuthority::invoke`]), which acknowledges
    /// delivery through this method; full domain work arrives with the
    /// services of Phase 7F.2.
    fn receive(&self, message: &BackboneMessage) -> DeliveryReceipt {
        DeliveryReceipt::delivered(message, 1)
    }

    /// Returns the service owned by this authority, if any.
    ///
    /// The controlled service-ownership surface: callers observe the owned
    /// service through this accessor only — there is no arbitrary mutable
    /// service collection to reach into. Phase 7F.2: every built-in
    /// authority owns the service of its domain; a service never belongs to
    /// another domain.
    fn service(&self) -> Option<&dyn Service> {
        None
    }

    /// The controlled service invocation boundary — the `Authority →
    /// Service` step of the communication path
    /// (`PlatformInterface → Backbone → Authority → Service →
    /// ServiceResult`).
    ///
    /// Called with the platform request the authority forwards to the
    /// service it owns. Contract:
    ///
    /// 1. the authority must be [`HubLifecycle::Active`] — a service must
    ///    not be reachable before its owning authority is Active, while it
    ///    is Suspended, or after it is Shutdown
    ///    ([`HubError::InactiveTarget`]);
    /// 2. delivery is acknowledged through the controlled delivery boundary
    ///    ([`HubAuthority::receive`]) — the boundary is never bypassed;
    /// 3. the authority must own a ready service
    ///    ([`HubError::ServiceUnavailable`]);
    /// 4. the owned service performs the work and returns its
    ///    [`ServiceResult`].
    ///
    /// The Active gate is the single service-availability boundary: a
    /// service executes domain operations only while its owning authority is
    /// Active (Phase 7F.5) — Suspended and Shutdown authorities reject
    /// invocation with [`HubError::InactiveTarget`].
    ///
    /// The invocation **acknowledges delivery itself** (step 2): callers
    /// invoke once — they must not pre-deliver the message through
    /// [`HubAuthority::receive`] and then invoke, or the authority
    /// acknowledges it twice. The invocation is addressed to this authority:
    /// the backbone resolves the target before delivery, and the authority
    /// trusts the backbone-resolved target.
    ///
    /// Phase 7F.2: every built-in authority owns the service of its domain;
    /// the [`HubError::ServiceUnavailable`] branch remains defensive for
    /// authorities that own no service.
    fn invoke(&self, invocation: &ServiceInvocation) -> HubResult<ServiceResult> {
        // 1. Active gate — inactive authorities never invoke services.
        if self.lifecycle() != HubLifecycle::Active {
            return Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(self.id()));
        }
        // 2. Delivery acknowledgment through the controlled boundary.
        let _ = self.receive(invocation.message());
        // 3. The owned service performs the domain work: it must be present
        //    and ready, and it must belong to this authority's domain — a
        //    service never belongs to another domain.
        let service = self
            .service()
            .ok_or(HubError::ServiceUnavailable(self.id()))?;
        if service.owner() != self.id() || !service.is_ready() {
            return Err(HubError::ServiceUnavailable(self.id()));
        }
        service.invoke(invocation)
    }
}

/// The Workspace Authority — the owner of the workspace domain.
///
/// Owns exactly one domain (workspace), composes the [`Hub`] metadata, is
/// born [`HubLifecycle::Registered`], exposes no domain operations and owns
/// the Workspace Service ([`WorkspaceService`], Phase 7F.2; Phase 7H: over
/// the platform storage root — the workspace domain persists its active
/// document and, since Phase 7H.1, its workspace object through the
/// existing Syss/PSS stack).
///
/// The authority is `Debug` only (like the Storage Authority): its service
/// owns the real storage stack, which is not `PartialEq`/`Clone`.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct WorkspaceAuthority {
    hub: Hub,
    lifecycle: HubLifecycle,
    service: Option<WorkspaceService>,
}

impl WorkspaceAuthority {
    /// Creates the Workspace Authority, born [`HubLifecycle::Registered`] and
    /// owning the Workspace Service over the platform default storage root.
    ///
    /// The frozen no-argument construction path, preserved for the default
    /// root and exercised by the tests; the boot chain uses
    /// [`WorkspaceAuthority::with_storage_root`] with the resolved platform
    /// root.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn new() -> WorkspaceAuthority {
        Self::with_storage_root(crate::syss::resolve_storage_root())
    }

    /// Creates the Workspace Authority owning the Workspace Service over the
    /// given storage root (Phase 7H, additive).
    ///
    /// The boot chain threads the resolved platform storage root down to the
    /// workspace boundary through this constructor (the workspace domain
    /// persists its active document through the existing Syss/PSS stack);
    /// the no-argument [`WorkspaceAuthority::new`] resolves the platform
    /// default root and remains the frozen construction path.
    pub(crate) fn with_storage_root(root: PathBuf) -> WorkspaceAuthority {
        WorkspaceAuthority {
            hub: Hub::new(HubDomain::Workspace),
            lifecycle: HubLifecycle::Registered,
            service: Some(WorkspaceService::with_root(root)),
        }
    }
}

impl HubAuthority for WorkspaceAuthority {
    fn id(&self) -> HubId {
        self.hub.id()
    }

    fn domain(&self) -> HubDomain {
        self.hub.domain()
    }

    fn hub(&self) -> &Hub {
        &self.hub
    }

    fn lifecycle(&self) -> HubLifecycle {
        self.lifecycle
    }

    fn set_lifecycle(&mut self, lifecycle: HubLifecycle) {
        self.lifecycle = lifecycle;
    }

    fn service(&self) -> Option<&dyn Service> {
        self.service.as_ref().map(|service| service as &dyn Service)
    }
}
