#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::hub::HubError;

    /// All eight concrete authorities as trait objects.
    fn all_authorities() -> Vec<Box<dyn HubAuthority>> {
        vec![
            Box::new(WorkspaceAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(ProjectAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(PackageAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(SettingsAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(HistoryAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(LogAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(StorageAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(DeviceAuthority::new()),
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_authority_owns_exactly_one_domain() {
        let workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        assert_eq!(workspace.id(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(workspace.domain(), HubDomain::Workspace);
        assert_eq!(workspace.hub().id(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(workspace.hub().domain(), HubDomain::Workspace);

        let storage = StorageAuthority::new();
        assert_eq!(storage.id(), HubId::STORAGE);
        assert_eq!(storage.domain(), HubDomain::Storage);
        assert_eq!(storage.hub().id(), HubId::STORAGE);
        assert_eq!(storage.hub().domain(), HubDomain::Storage);
    }

    #[test]
    fn authorities_mirror_the_initial_hub_set() {
        let authorities = all_authorities();
        assert_eq!(authorities.len(), HubId::ALL.len());

        // Every stable hub id has exactly one authority, and every authority
        // owns exactly one distinct domain.
        //
        // Comparing against `ALL` relies on the derived `Ord` (enum
        // declaration order) matching the declaration order of `ALL`; both
        // follow the same domain vocabulary, so the sorted vectors must equal
        // the constants exactly.
        let mut ids: Vec<HubId> = authorities.iter().map(|a| a.id()).collect();
        ids.sort();
        ids.dedup();
        assert_eq!(ids, HubId::ALL);

        let mut domains: Vec<HubDomain> = authorities.iter().map(|a| a.domain()).collect();
        domains.sort();
        domains.dedup();
        assert_eq!(domains, HubDomain::ALL);

        // id and domain correspond one-to-one for every authority.
        for authority in &authorities {
            assert_eq!(authority.id(), HubId::from_domain(authority.domain()));
            assert_eq!(authority.hub().id(), authority.id());
            assert_eq!(authority.hub().domain(), authority.domain());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn authorities_are_born_registered() {
        assert_eq!(
            WorkspaceAuthority::new().lifecycle(),
            HubLifecycle::Registered
        );
        assert_eq!(
            StorageAuthority::new().lifecycle(),
            HubLifecycle::Registered
        );
        assert_eq!(DeviceAuthority::new().lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Registered);
        for authority in all_authorities() {
            assert_eq!(authority.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Registered);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn registration_with_the_registry_round_trips() {
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        WorkspaceAuthority::new().register(&mut registry).unwrap();

        assert!(registry.contains(HubId::WORKSPACE));
        assert_eq!(
            registry.lookup(HubId::WORKSPACE).map(|hub| hub.domain()),
            Some(HubDomain::Workspace)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn duplicate_registration_is_rejected() {
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        let settings = SettingsAuthority::new();
        settings.register(&mut registry).unwrap();
        let err = settings.register(&mut registry).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err, HubError::AlreadyRegistered(HubId::SETTINGS));
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_authority_registers_under_its_own_id() {
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        for authority in all_authorities() {
            authority.register(&mut registry).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(registry.len(), HubId::ALL.len());
        for id in HubId::ALL {
            assert!(registry.contains(id));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn initialize_transitions_registered_to_initialized() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Registered);
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Initialized);
    }

    #[test]
    fn activate_transitions_initialized_to_active() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Active);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_full_startup_chain_reaches_active() {
        for mut authority in all_authorities() {
            authority.initialize().unwrap();
            authority.activate().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(authority.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Active);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn initialize_rejects_a_non_registered_state() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        // Already Initialized: the startup transition must reject it.
        let err = workspace.initialize().unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            err,
            HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Initialized,
                to: HubLifecycle::Initialized,
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn activate_rejects_a_non_initialized_state() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        // Still Registered: activation requires Initialized first.
        let err = workspace.activate().unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            err,
            HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Registered,
                to: HubLifecycle::Active,
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn startup_chain_runs_after_registration() {
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        let mut activated: Vec<Box<dyn HubAuthority>> = all_authorities();
        for authority in activated.iter_mut() {
            authority.register(&mut registry).unwrap();
            authority.initialize().unwrap();
            authority.activate().unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(registry.len(), HubId::ALL.len());
        for authority in &activated {
            assert_eq!(authority.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Active);
        }
    }
    #[test]
    fn authorities_acknowledge_backbone_delivery() {
        let log = LogAuthority::new();
        let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Notification,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        let receipt = log.receive(&message);
        assert_eq!(
            receipt.status(),
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneStatus::Delivered
        );
        assert_eq!(
            receipt.kind(),
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Notification
        );
        assert_eq!(receipt.source(), HubId::DEVICE);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::LOG));
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 1);
    }

    fn log_request() -> crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage {
        crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_log_authority_owns_the_log_service() {
        let log = LogAuthority::new();
        let service = log.service().expect("log authority owns the log service");
        assert_eq!(service.id().name(), "log");
        assert_eq!(service.owner(), HubId::LOG);
        assert!(service.is_ready());
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_authority_owns_the_service_of_its_domain() {
        let pairs: [(HubId, &str); 8] = [
            (HubId::WORKSPACE, "workspace"),
            (HubId::PROJECT, "project"),
            (HubId::PACKAGE, "package"),
            (HubId::SETTINGS, "settings"),
            (HubId::HISTORY, "history"),
            (HubId::LOG, "log"),
            (HubId::STORAGE, "storage"),
            (HubId::DEVICE, "device"),
        ];
        for (hub, name) in pairs {
            let authority = all_authorities()
                .into_iter()
                .find(|authority| authority.id() == hub)
                .expect("authority exists");
            let service = authority
                .service()
                .expect("every authority owns the service of its domain");
            assert_eq!(
                service.owner(),
                hub,
                "{name} service must be owned by {hub}"
            );
            assert_eq!(service.id().name(), name);
            assert!(service.is_ready());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_service_never_belongs_to_another_domain() {
        for authority in all_authorities() {
            let service = authority.service().unwrap();
            // The authority's own service belongs to its domain, never to
            // any other domain.
            assert_eq!(service.owner(), authority.id());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_active_authority_invokes_its_owned_service() {
        let mut authorities = all_authorities();
        for authority in authorities.iter_mut() {
            authority.initialize().unwrap();
            authority.activate().unwrap();
        }
        for authority in authorities.iter() {
            let hub = authority.id();
            let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
                crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                HubId::DEVICE,
                Some(hub),
            );
            let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
            // The Log proof service and the domain services both complete a
            // command.
            assert_eq!(
                authority.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(),
                ServiceResult::Completed,
                "authority {hub} must invoke its owned service"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_inactive_authority_prevents_service_invocation() {
        // Authorities are born Registered: their services must not be
        // reachable until the authority is Active.
        for authority in all_authorities() {
            let hub = authority.id();
            let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
                crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                HubId::DEVICE,
                Some(hub),
            );
            let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
            assert_eq!(
                authority.invoke(&invocation),
                Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(hub)),
                "authority {hub} must reject invocation while inactive"
            );
        }
    }
    #[test]
    fn active_authority_forwards_the_request_to_its_service() {
        let mut log = LogAuthority::new();
        log.initialize().unwrap();
        log.activate().unwrap();
        let message = log_request();
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(log.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(), ServiceResult::Completed);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inactive_authority_prevents_service_invocation() {
        // The Log Authority is born Registered: its service must not be
        // reachable until the authority is Active.
        let log = LogAuthority::new();
        let message = log_request();
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(
            log.invoke(&invocation),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::LOG))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_log_authority_invokes_its_proof_service() {
        // The Log Authority keeps the Phase 7F.1 proof service; its
        // invocation behavior is preserved.
        let mut log = LogAuthority::new();
        log.initialize().unwrap();
        log.activate().unwrap();
        let message = log_request();
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(log.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(), ServiceResult::Completed);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_active_authority_forwards_real_domain_operations() {
        // Phase 7F.3: the authority forwards real domain operations to its
        // owned service, which carries domain state and answers questions
        // with the synchronous Response. The authority runs over an isolated
        // storage root (opening the workspace persists its state).
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h1-authority");
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned());
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        let open = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(crate::hub::BackbonePayload::Operation(
            crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
        ));
        let open_invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&open);
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&open_invocation).unwrap(),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        let inspect = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(crate::hub::BackbonePayload::Operation(
            crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
        ));
        let inspect_invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&inspect);
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&inspect_invocation).unwrap(),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("workspace: ra-main".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn suspend_transitions_active_to_suspended() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Suspended);
    }

    #[test]
    fn resume_transitions_suspended_to_active() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        workspace.resume().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Active);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shutdown_transitions_active_to_shutdown() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Shutdown);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shutdown_transitions_suspended_to_shutdown() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        workspace.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Shutdown);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_full_lifecycle_chain_is_validated() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        // Registered → Initialized → Active → Suspended → Active → Shutdown.
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        workspace.resume().unwrap();
        workspace.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Shutdown);
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_lifecycle_transitions_are_rejected() {
        // Registered → Active: activation requires Initialized first.
        let mut registered = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        assert_eq!(
            registered.activate(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Registered,
                to: HubLifecycle::Active,
            })
        );
        // Registered → Suspended: suspension requires Active.
        let mut registered = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        assert_eq!(
            registered.suspend(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Registered,
                to: HubLifecycle::Suspended,
            })
        );
        // Initialized → Suspended: suspension requires Active.
        let mut initialized = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        initialized.initialize().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            initialized.suspend(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Initialized,
                to: HubLifecycle::Suspended,
            })
        );
        // Initialized → Shutdown: shutdown requires Active or Suspended.
        let mut initialized = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        initialized.initialize().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            initialized.shutdown(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Initialized,
                to: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
            })
        );
        // Shutdown is terminal: nothing leaves it.
        let mut shutdown = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        shutdown.initialize().unwrap();
        shutdown.activate().unwrap();
        shutdown.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            shutdown.initialize(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                to: HubLifecycle::Initialized,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            shutdown.activate(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                to: HubLifecycle::Active,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            shutdown.suspend(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                to: HubLifecycle::Suspended,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            shutdown.resume(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                to: HubLifecycle::Active,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            shutdown.shutdown(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                to: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn services_are_unavailable_while_the_authority_is_suspended() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        // Suspension pauses the domain: services must not execute normal
        // operations while the owning authority is Suspended.
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&invocation),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::WORKSPACE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn services_are_unavailable_after_shutdown() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.shutdown().unwrap();
        let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        // Shutdown terminates the domain: services can never execute again.
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&invocation),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::WORKSPACE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn suspension_preserves_the_domain_state_for_resume() {
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h1-authority-suspend");
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned());
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        // Open the workspace (real domain state, Phase 7F.3).
        let open = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(crate::hub::BackbonePayload::Operation(
            crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&ServiceInvocation::new(&open)).unwrap(),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Suspend and resume: the domain state must survive intact.
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        workspace.resume().unwrap();
        let inspect = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(crate::hub::BackbonePayload::Operation(
            crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&ServiceInvocation::new(&inspect)).unwrap(),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("workspace: ra-main".to_owned())
        );
    }
}

=== KERNEL ===
//! Platform Kernel initialization (Phase 7D.3).
//!
//! The **Platform Kernel** is the live core of the SySS platform: the
//! registry of hub authorities that the platform runs on. This module brings
//! it online — **startup orchestration only**, no business logic.
//!
//! The boot chain after Phase 7D.3:
//!
//! `SySS::initialize → Platform Kernel Initialization → Platform Ready`
//!
//! # Components
//!
//! * [`BuiltinAuthorities`] — the eight built-in hub authorities, one per
//!   initial domain (created in Phase 7D.2).
//! * [`Kernel`] — the initialized kernel: the authority registry, the hub
//!   graph and router contracts, and the built-in authorities, with a
//!   readiness check.
//! * [`KernelInitializer`] — owns the startup orchestration: creates the
//!   authorities, registers them with the [`Registry`], runs the startup
//!   lifecycle transitions (`Registered → Initialized → Active`) and verifies
//!   kernel readiness.
//!
//! # Scope
//!
//! Orchestration only. No services, no active objects and no RA Core
//! initialization — those are later phases. Phase 7F.5 adds the **aggregate
//! lifecycle control**: the kernel suspends, resumes and shuts down the
//! whole authority set together ([`Kernel::suspend`], [`Kernel::resume`],
//! [`Kernel::shutdown`]) — the kernel remains the owner of aggregate
//! platform lifecycle control.
//!
//! # Platform Backbone (Phase 7E)
//!
//! The kernel is the **home of the Platform Backbone**: it owns the routing
//! contracts the backbone consumes — the [`HubGraph`] topology and the
//! [`Router`] — alongside the hub [`Registry`] and the
//! [`BuiltinAuthorities`]. [`Kernel::backbone`] produces the backbone view
//! over those contracts, and [`Kernel::is_ready`] verifies the backbone is
//! attached and operational as part of readiness (Platform Ready). The
//! backbone implements the Phase 7E.1 communication runtime — validation,
//! target resolution and delivery — with no business logic; Phase 7F.1
//! attaches the Service abstraction and the Log proof service behind the
//! authorities without touching the kernel ownership (TODO(Phase7F.2) for
//! the full domain services).

use std::path::PathBuf;

use super::{
    DeviceAuthority, HistoryAuthority, HubAuthority, HubError, HubGraph, HubId, HubLifecycle,
    HubResult, LogAuthority, PackageAuthority, PlatformBackbone, ProjectAuthority, Registry,
    Router, SettingsAuthority, StorageAuthority, WorkspaceAuthority,
};

/// The eight built-in hub authorities of the platform kernel, one per
/// initial domain.
///
/// This is the **authority set** the kernel is created from. Each built-in
/// authority is a concrete type owning exactly one domain; the set exposes
/// uniform iteration over all of them through the [`HubAuthority`] contract.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct BuiltinAuthorities {
    workspace: WorkspaceAuthority,
    project: ProjectAuthority,
    package: PackageAuthority,
    settings: SettingsAuthority,
    history: HistoryAuthority,
    log: LogAuthority,
    storage: StorageAuthority,
    device: DeviceAuthority,
}

impl BuiltinAuthorities {
    /// Creates the eight built-in authorities, each born
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Registered`], over the platform default storage root.
    ///
    /// No future authorities (Execution, Database) are created here. The
    /// frozen no-argument construction path, preserved for the default root
    /// and exercised by the tests; the boot chain uses
    /// [`BuiltinAuthorities::with_storage_root`] with the resolved platform
    /// root.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn new() -> BuiltinAuthorities {
        Self::with_storage_root(crate::syss::resolve_storage_root())
    }

    /// Creates the eight built-in authorities over the given storage root
    /// (Phase 7G.1, additive; Phase 7H.1 threads the root to the project and
    /// package boundaries too; Phase 7H.2 threads it to the settings,
    /// history and log boundaries).
    ///
    /// The boot chain threads the resolved platform storage root down to the
    /// storage boundary through this constructor; the no-argument
    /// [`BuiltinAuthorities::new`] resolves the platform default root and
    /// remains the frozen construction path. The authorities whose domains
    /// persist through the existing Syss/PSS stack — the Workspace
    /// (documents and the workspace object), the Project, the Package, the
    /// Settings, the History, the Log and the Storage Authority — consume
    /// the root; only the Device Authority owns no persisted state.
    pub(crate) fn with_storage_root(root: PathBuf) -> BuiltinAuthorities {
        BuiltinAuthorities {
            workspace: WorkspaceAuthority::with_storage_root(root.clone()),
            project: ProjectAuthority::with_storage_root(root.clone()),
            package: PackageAuthority::with_storage_root(root.clone()),
            settings: SettingsAuthority::with_storage_root(root.clone()),
            history: HistoryAuthority::with_storage_root(root.clone()),
            log: LogAuthority::with_storage_root(root.clone()),
            storage: StorageAuthority::with_storage_root(root),
            device: DeviceAuthority::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Iterates over all built-in authorities.
    pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &dyn HubAuthority> {
        [
            &self.workspace as &dyn HubAuthority,
            &self.project as &dyn HubAuthority,
            &self.package as &dyn HubAuthority,
            &self.settings as &dyn HubAuthority,
            &self.history as &dyn HubAuthority,
            &self.log as &dyn HubAuthority,
            &self.storage as &dyn HubAuthority,
            &self.device as &dyn HubAuthority,
        ]
        .into_iter()
    }

    /// Mutably iterates over all built-in authorities.
    pub(crate) fn iter_mut(&mut self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &mut dyn HubAuthority> {
        [
            &mut self.workspace as &mut dyn HubAuthority,
            &mut self.project as &mut dyn HubAuthority,
            &mut self.package as &mut dyn HubAuthority,
            &mut self.settings as &mut dyn HubAuthority,
            &mut self.history as &mut dyn HubAuthority,
            &mut self.log as &mut dyn HubAuthority,
            &mut self.storage as &mut dyn HubAuthority,
            &mut self.device as &mut dyn HubAuthority,
        ]
        .into_iter()
    }

    /// Returns whether all built-in authorities are in `lifecycle`.
    fn all_in(&self, lifecycle: HubLifecycle) -> bool {
        self.iter()
            .all(|authority| authority.lifecycle() == lifecycle)
    }

    /// Applies the validated transition to `to` on **every** built-in
    /// authority (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// All-or-nothing: every authority must be in a state that allows `to`
    /// under the single transition table
    /// ([`HubLifecycle::can_transition`]) before **any** authority
    /// transitions — a single authority never transitions independently in
    /// a way that leaves the platform in an inconsistent state. The
    /// per-authority named transitions
    /// ([`HubAuthority::suspend`](crate::hub::HubAuthority::suspend),
    /// [`HubAuthority::resume`](crate::hub::HubAuthority::resume),
    /// [`HubAuthority::shutdown`](crate::hub::HubAuthority::shutdown)) are
    /// the single validation point; this helper only guarantees the
    /// aggregate atomicity.
    fn transition_all(&mut self, to: HubLifecycle) -> HubResult<()> {
        // Validate every authority first (deterministic order, no partial
        // application on failure).
        for authority in self.iter() {
            if !authority.lifecycle().can_transition(to) {
                return Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                    from: authority.lifecycle(),
                    to,
                });
            }
        }
        // Then apply the named transition to every authority. The kernel
        // drives the post-startup lifecycle transitions only: registration
        // and the startup transitions are the initializer's job.
        for authority in self.iter_mut() {
            match to {
                HubLifecycle::Suspended => authority.suspend()?,
                HubLifecycle::Active => authority.resume()?,
                HubLifecycle::Shutdown => authority.shutdown()?,
                HubLifecycle::Registered | HubLifecycle::Initialized => {
                    // Unreachable after the validation loop above (no
                    // Active/Suspended authority may transition to
                    // Registered/Initialized); defensive and deterministic.
                    return Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                        from: authority.lifecycle(),
                        to,
                    });
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The initialized Platform Kernel.
///
/// Owns the built-in hub authorities, their [`Registry`], and the hub
/// [`HubGraph`] and [`Router`] contracts the Platform Backbone consumes. The
/// graph carries its own registry — the topology-knowledge record of the same
/// hub set the kernel's registry holds (the kernel's registry is the
/// canonical hub table). The kernel is the *result* of startup — it is only
/// produced by the [`KernelInitializer`] after registration, initialization,
/// activation and a readiness check; it is not `Copy` (a running kernel has
/// exactly one owner).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Kernel {
    registry: Registry,
    graph: HubGraph,
    router: Router,
    authorities: BuiltinAuthorities,
}

impl Kernel {
    /// Assembles a kernel from the given contracts and authorities.
    ///
    /// Used by the [`KernelInitializer`] once the authorities are registered,
    /// initialized and activated, and the hub graph and router are in place.
    /// Readiness is **not** checked here — call [`Kernel::is_ready`] to
    /// verify.
    pub(crate) fn new(
        registry: Registry,
        graph: HubGraph,
        router: Router,
        authorities: BuiltinAuthorities,
    ) -> Kernel {
        Kernel {
            registry,
            graph,
            router,
            authorities,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the hub registry of the kernel.
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests and Platform Services
    /// read the registry through this accessor (TODO(Phase7F)).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn registry(&self) -> &Registry {
        &self.registry
    }

    /// Returns the built-in authorities of the kernel.
    ///
    /// Read by the Phase 7F.1 service probe ([`crate::SySS::probe_service`])
    /// and the tests to reach an authority and its owned service.
    pub(crate) fn authorities(&self) -> &BuiltinAuthorities {
        &self.authorities
    }

    /// Returns the Platform Backbone over the kernel's communication
    /// contracts.
    ///
    /// The backbone view borrows the kernel's hub [`Registry`], [`HubGraph`]
    /// topology, [`Router`] and [`BuiltinAuthorities`]; the kernel owns them,
    /// the backbone consumes them. The view is short-lived — recreate it for
    /// each use.
    pub(crate) fn backbone(&self) -> PlatformBackbone<'_> {
        PlatformBackbone::attach(&self.registry, &self.graph, &self.router, &self.authorities)
    }

    /// Returns the lifecycle state of the built-in authority with `id`, if
    /// present among the kernel's authorities.
    ///
    /// The kernel's authorities are the built-in set; a freshly assembled
    /// kernel built through [`KernelInitializer`] has every authority
    /// registered, but this lookup itself searches the authority set, not the
    /// registry.
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests and Platform Services
    /// query per-hub lifecycle through this accessor (TODO(Phase7F)).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn lifecycle_of(&self, id: HubId) -> Option<HubLifecycle> {
        self.authorities
            .iter()
            .find(|authority| authority.id() == id)
            .map(|authority| authority.lifecycle())
    }

    /// Suspends the whole platform: every built-in authority transitions
    /// `Active → Suspended` (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// Aggregate lifecycle control — the kernel is the owner of aggregate
    /// platform lifecycle. All-or-nothing: either every authority suspends
    /// or none does ([`BuiltinAuthorities::transition_all`]). Suspension is
    /// **pause, not shutdown**: domain state is preserved, and the backbone
    /// gate (dispatch resolves only `Active` authorities) rejects normal
    /// traffic while the platform is suspended.
    pub(crate) fn suspend(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.authorities.transition_all(HubLifecycle::Suspended)
    }

    /// Resumes the whole platform: every built-in authority transitions
    /// `Suspended → Active` (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// The domain state preserved during suspension remains available, and
    /// the backbone gate routes and delivers normally again. All-or-nothing.
    pub(crate) fn resume(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.authorities.transition_all(HubLifecycle::Active)
    }

    /// Shuts the platform kernel down: every built-in authority transitions
    /// `Active | Suspended → Shutdown` (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// Deterministic, synchronous teardown of the authority set — all-or-
    /// nothing ([`BuiltinAuthorities::transition_all`]); [`HubLifecycle::Shutdown`]
    /// is terminal, so a second aggregate shutdown is rejected (the kernel
    /// shuts down once). After shutdown no authority is `Active`, so the
    /// backbone gate rejects every normal platform message: no new requests
    /// are accepted, and no service can execute again.
    pub(crate) fn shutdown(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.authorities.transition_all(HubLifecycle::Shutdown)
    }

    /// Verifies kernel readiness: every built-in authority exists in the
    /// registry, the registry is complete, every authority is
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Active`], and the Platform Backbone is attached and
    /// operational (its runtime operations — validation, resolution and
    /// delivery — succeed on the authority set).
    pub(crate) fn is_ready(&self) -> bool {
        let registry_complete = self.registry.len() == HubId::ALL.len()
            && self
                .authorities
                .iter()
                .all(|authority| self.registry.contains(authority.id()));
        let mut backbone = self.backbone();
        registry_complete
            && self.authorities.all_in(HubLifecycle::Active)
            && backbone.is_attached()
            && backbone.is_operational()
    }
}

/// The Platform Kernel Initializer — owns the startup orchestration.
///
/// Brings the platform kernel online: creates the built-in authorities,
/// registers them with a fresh [`Registry`], builds the hub graph and router
/// the Platform Backbone consumes, runs the startup lifecycle transitions
/// (`Registered → Initialized → Active`) and verifies kernel readiness.
/// **Orchestration only** — no business logic and no services; backbone
/// dispatch is exercised only through the readiness check.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub(crate) struct KernelInitializer;

impl KernelInitializer {
    /// Creates the Platform Kernel Initializer.
    pub(crate) fn new() -> KernelInitializer {
        KernelInitializer
    }

    /// Initializes the platform kernel and returns it ready, over the
    /// platform default storage root.
    ///
    /// Delegates to [`initialize_with_storage`](KernelInitializer::initialize_with_storage)
    /// with the resolved default root — the frozen no-argument startup path,
    /// preserved for the default root and exercised by the tests; the boot
    /// chain uses [`KernelInitializer::initialize_with_storage`] with the
    /// resolved platform root.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn initialize(&self) -> HubResult<Kernel> {
        self.initialize_with_storage(crate::syss::resolve_storage_root())
    }

    /// Initializes the platform kernel over the given storage root and
    /// returns it ready (Phase 7G.1, additive).
    ///
    /// The boot chain threads the resolved platform storage root down to the
    /// storage boundary through this constructor; the no-argument
    /// [`KernelInitializer::initialize`] resolves the platform default root
    /// and remains the frozen startup path.
    ///
    /// Steps, in order:
    /// 1. **Create** the eight built-in authorities (the Storage Authority
    ///    over the given root).
    /// 2. **Register** every authority with the [`Registry`] (existing
    ///    registration contracts; no duplicated logic).
    /// 3. **Initialize** every authority (`Registered → Initialized`).
    /// 4. **Activate** every authority (`Initialized → Active`).
    /// 5. **Build the backbone contracts** — the [`HubGraph`] topology (the
    ///    kernel's knowledge of the authority set) and the [`Router`] the
    ///    Platform Backbone consumes.
    /// 6. **Verify** kernel readiness — every authority exists, the registry
    ///    is complete, every authority is `Active`, and the Platform Backbone
    ///    is attached — failing with [`HubError::KernelNotReady`] otherwise.
    ///
    /// On success the returned [`Kernel`] is **Platform Ready**.
    pub(crate) fn initialize_with_storage(&self, root: PathBuf) -> HubResult<Kernel> {
        // 1. Create the built-in authorities.
        let mut authorities = BuiltinAuthorities::with_storage_root(root);

        // 2. Register every authority with the registry.
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        for authority in authorities.iter_mut() {
            authority.register(&mut registry)?;
        }

        // 3. Initialize every authority (Registered → Initialized).
        for authority in authorities.iter_mut() {
            authority.initialize()?;
        }

        // 4. Activate every authority (Initialized → Active).
        for authority in authorities.iter_mut() {
            authority.activate()?;
        }

        // 5. Build the backbone contracts: the hub graph (the kernel's
        //    topology knowledge) and the router.
        let mut graph = HubGraph::new();
        for authority in authorities.iter() {
            graph.register(*authority.hub())?;
        }
        let router = Router::new();

        // 6. Assemble the kernel and verify readiness.
        let kernel = Kernel::new(registry, graph, router, authorities);
        if !kernel.is_ready() {
            return Err(HubError::KernelNotReady);
        }
        Ok(kernel)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::hub::backbone::Backbone;

    #[test]
    fn builtin_authorities_cover_every_initial_domain() {
        let authorities = BuiltinAuthorities::new();
        let ids: Vec<HubId> = authorities.iter().map(|a| a.id()).collect();
        assert_eq!(ids.len(), HubId::ALL.len());
        for id in HubId::ALL {
            assert!(ids.contains(&id), "missing built-in authority for {id}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn builtin_authorities_are_born_registered() {
        let authorities = BuiltinAuthorities::new();
        assert!(authorities.all_in(HubLifecycle::Registered));
    }

    #[test]
    fn initializer_brings_the_kernel_online() {
        let kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        assert!(kernel.is_ready(), "kernel must be platform ready");
    }

    #[test]
    fn initializer_with_storage_brings_the_kernel_online() {
        // Phase 7G.1 additive path: the kernel can be brought online over an
        // explicit storage root, threaded down to the Storage Authority.
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7g1-kernel");
        let kernel = KernelInitializer::new()
            .initialize_with_storage(dir.path().to_owned())
            .unwrap();
        assert!(kernel.is_ready(), "kernel must be platform ready");
        for authority in kernel.authorities().iter() {
            assert_eq!(authority.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Active);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn initializer_registers_every_authority() {
        let kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(kernel.registry().len(), HubId::ALL.len());
        for id in HubId::ALL {
            assert!(
                kernel.registry().contains(id),
                "registry missing authority {id}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn initializer_activates_every_authority() {
        let kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        for authority in kernel.authorities().iter() {
            assert_eq!(
                authority.lifecycle(),
                HubLifecycle::Active,
                "authority {} not active",
                authority.id()
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn kernel_is_not_ready_without_activation() {
        // Fresh authorities are registered but never initialized/activated.
        let mut authorities = BuiltinAuthorities::new();
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        for authority in authorities.iter_mut() {
            authority.register(&mut registry).unwrap();
        }
        let mut graph = HubGraph::new();
        for authority in authorities.iter() {
            graph.register(*authority.hub()).unwrap();
        }
        let kernel = Kernel::new(registry, graph, Router::new(), authorities);
        assert!(!kernel.is_ready());
    }

    #[test]
    fn kernel_exposes_an_attached_and_operational_backbone() {
        let kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        assert!(
            backbone.is_attached(),
            "the Platform Backbone must be attached to a ready kernel"
        );
        assert!(
            backbone.is_operational(),
            "the Platform Backbone must be operational on a ready kernel"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn lifecycle_of_reports_the_authority_state() {
        let kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            kernel.lifecycle_of(HubId::WORKSPACE),
            Some(HubLifecycle::Active)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            kernel.lifecycle_of(HubId::DEVICE),
            Some(HubLifecycle::Active)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_kernel_suspends_all_authorities_together() {
        let mut kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        kernel.suspend().unwrap();
        for authority in kernel.authorities().iter() {
            assert_eq!(
                authority.lifecycle(),
                HubLifecycle::Suspended,
                "authority {} must suspend together with the platform",
                authority.id()
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_kernel_resumes_all_authorities_together() {
        let mut kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        kernel.suspend().unwrap();
        kernel.resume().unwrap();
        for authority in kernel.authorities().iter() {
            assert_eq!(
                authority.lifecycle(),
                HubLifecycle::Active,
                "authority {} must resume together with the platform",
                authority.id()
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_kernel_shuts_down_all_authorities() {
        let mut kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        kernel.shutdown().unwrap();
        for authority in kernel.authorities().iter() {
            assert_eq!(
                authority.lifecycle(),
                HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                "authority {} must shut down with the platform",
                authority.id()
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_kernel_shuts_down_once() {
        let mut kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        kernel.shutdown().unwrap();
        // Shutdown is terminal: a second aggregate shutdown is rejected
        // deterministically — no authority can leave Shutdown.
        assert!(kernel.shutdown().is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_kernel_suspends_once() {
        let mut kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        kernel.suspend().unwrap();
        // Double suspension is rejected: Suspended → Suspended is not a
        // valid transition.
        assert!(kernel.suspend().is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_kernel_shuts_down_from_suspended() {
        let mut kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        kernel.suspend().unwrap();
        kernel.shutdown().unwrap();
        for authority in kernel.authorities().iter() {
            assert_eq!(authority.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Shutdown);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_suspended_kernel_is_not_ready_or_operational() {
        let mut kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        kernel.suspend().unwrap();
        assert!(!kernel.is_ready());
        assert!(!kernel.backbone().is_operational());
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_rejects_normal_traffic_while_the_kernel_is_suspended() {
        let mut kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        kernel.suspend().unwrap();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        // No authority is Active while suspended: the backbone gate rejects
        // the normal request instead of fabricating a delivery.
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::WORKSPACE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_rejects_normal_traffic_after_kernel_shutdown() {
        let mut kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        kernel.shutdown().unwrap();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        // After shutdown no authority is Active: new requests are blocked
        // and no delivery receipt is fabricated.
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::LOG))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_rejects_storage_traffic_after_shutdown() {
        // Phase 7G lifecycle invariant: platform Stopped → storage
        // unavailable. After the kernel shuts down, a storage request is
        // rejected by the backbone gate (the Storage Authority is Shutdown
        // and never Active again) — no new storage operations enter the
        // platform.
        let mut kernel = KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap();
        kernel.shutdown().unwrap();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::STORAGE),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::STORAGE))
        );
    }
}

=== HUB ID / DOMAIN ===
//! Stable hub identifiers.
//!
//! [`HubId`] is the identity token of a hub slot in the SySS hub graph. The
//! registry, the graph and routing refer to hubs exclusively by id; the id
//! vocabulary is stable and an id is never reused.

use std::fmt;

use super::hub::HubDomain;

/// The stable identifier of a hub slot in the SySS hub graph.
///
/// A [`HubId`] is **opaque**: its underlying representation is private, and
/// ids are obtained only through the documented constants ([`HubId::ALL`] and
/// the per-hub constants). Callers can compare ids, hash them, print them and
/// ask for their stable name, but never construct one from arbitrary data.
///
/// There is exactly one id per [`HubDomain`], and an id is never reused: a
/// hub that is unregistered is gone for good.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub(crate) struct HubId {
    domain: HubDomain,
}

impl HubId {
    /// The Workspace Hub — the authority for the workspace domain.
    pub(crate) const WORKSPACE: HubId = HubId {
        domain: HubDomain::Workspace,
    };
    /// The Project Hub — the authority for the project domain.
    pub(crate) const PROJECT: HubId = HubId {
        domain: HubDomain::Project,
    };
    /// The Package Hub — the authority for the package domain.
    pub(crate) const PACKAGE: HubId = HubId {
        domain: HubDomain::Package,
    };
    /// The Settings Hub — the authority for the settings domain.
    pub(crate) const SETTINGS: HubId = HubId {
        domain: HubDomain::Settings,
    };
    /// The History Hub — the authority for the history domain.
    pub(crate) const HISTORY: HubId = HubId {
        domain: HubDomain::History,
    };
    /// The Log Hub — the authority for the log domain.
    pub(crate) const LOG: HubId = HubId {
        domain: HubDomain::Log,
    };
    /// The Storage Hub — the authority for the storage domain.
    pub(crate) const STORAGE: HubId = HubId {
        domain: HubDomain::Storage,
    };
    /// The Device Hub — the authority for the device domain.
    pub(crate) const DEVICE: HubId = HubId {
        domain: HubDomain::Device,
    };

    /// All initial hub identifiers, in stable order.
    ///
    /// The Execution Hub and the Database Hub are future expansion points and
    /// are deliberately absent here.
    pub(crate) const ALL: [HubId; 8] = [
        HubId::WORKSPACE,
        HubId::PROJECT,
        HubId::PACKAGE,
        HubId::SETTINGS,
        HubId::HISTORY,
        HubId::LOG,
        HubId::STORAGE,
        HubId::DEVICE,
    ];

    /// Returns the stable name of this hub ("workspace", "project", ...).
    pub(crate) fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        self.domain.name()
    }

    /// Returns the platform domain this hub is the authority for.
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests and later phases use it
    /// (TODO(Phase7F)).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn domain(self) -> HubDomain {
        self.domain
    }

    /// Returns the hub id that is the authority for `domain`.
    ///
    /// Crate-internal: hub ids are constructed only from their domain (each
    /// hub owns exactly one domain), never from arbitrary data.
    pub(crate) const fn from_domain(domain: HubDomain) -> HubId {
        HubId { domain }
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for HubId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.name())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn all_has_eight_initial_hubs() {
        assert_eq!(HubId::ALL.len(), 8);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ids_are_pairwise_distinct() {
        for (i, a) in HubId::ALL.iter().enumerate() {
            for (j, b) in HubId::ALL.iter().enumerate() {
                if i != j {
                    assert_ne!(a, b, "ids {a} and {b} collide");
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn names_are_stable_and_printable() {
        let names: Vec<&str> = HubId::ALL.iter().map(|id| id.name()).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            names,
            vec![
                "workspace",
                "project",
                "package",
                "settings",
                "history",
                "log",
                "storage",
                "device",
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(HubId::STORAGE.to_string(), "storage");
    }

    #[test]
    fn ids_own_exactly_one_domain() {
        for id in HubId::ALL {
            assert_eq!(HubId::from_domain(id.domain()), id);
        }
    }
}

=== HUB MODULE ===
//! The SySS Hub Graph (Phases 7D.1–7D.3, 7E — contracts, hub authorities,
//! the Platform Kernel and the Platform Backbone).
//!
//! The Hub Graph is the **internal topology of the Platform Kernel**. It is
//! the Phase 7D home of the hub contracts: hub identifiers, hub domains, the
//! hub lifecycle vocabulary, the hub registry, the hub graph knowledge and
//! the routing contracts.
//!
//! The Hub Graph lives **inside** `ra-syss` (it is not a separate crate) and
//! is **never exposed** through the public platform surface
//! ([`crate::PlatformInterface`]): consumers of the platform see only the
//! platform interface, never the graph. Everything in this module is
//! `pub(crate)` — internal scaffolding for the Platform Kernel.
//!
//! # Hub ownership
//!
//! * A Hub **owns exactly one platform domain** ([`HubDomain`]).
//! * A Hub is the **single authority** for that domain: no two Hubs own the
//!   same responsibility ([`HubGraph::authority_for`]).
//! * A Hub **performs no business logic**.
//! * Hubs **never communicate directly**; every interaction is coordinated
//!   through SySS infrastructure — the **Platform Backbone** (the `backbone`
//!   module), the single communication path of the platform.
//!
//! # Initial hubs
//!
//! The contracts define the eight initial hubs, one per domain:
//!
//! | Hub id | Domain |
//! |--------|--------|
//! | [`HubId::WORKSPACE`] | [`HubDomain::Workspace`] |
//! | [`HubId::PROJECT`] | [`HubDomain::Project`] |
//! | [`HubId::PACKAGE`] | [`HubDomain::Package`] |
//! | [`HubId::SETTINGS`] | [`HubDomain::Settings`] |
//! | [`HubId::HISTORY`] | [`HubDomain::History`] |
//! | [`HubId::LOG`] | [`HubDomain::Log`] |
//! | [`HubId::STORAGE`] | [`HubDomain::Storage`] |
//! | [`HubId::DEVICE`] | [`HubDomain::Device`] |
//!
//! The **Execution Hub** and the **Database Hub** are documented as **future
//! expansion points only**: they are named here but are not part of the
//! initial hub set, and will be added together with the Execution Manager and
//! the Database in later phases.
//!
//! # Registration
//!
//! The [`Registry`] is the hub table of the graph. Its surface is
//! deliberately narrow — **registration and lookup contracts only**:
//!
//! * registration: [`Registry::register`] / [`Registry::unregister`];
//! * lookup: [`Registry::lookup`], [`Registry::contains`], [`Registry::hubs`].
//!
//! A hub id is unique and never reused; registering the same id twice fails
//! with [`HubError::AlreadyRegistered`].
//!
//! # Authorities (Phase 7D.2)
//!
//! The concrete per-domain hub objects are the **hub authorities** (the
//! `authority` module): one [`HubAuthority`] per initial domain, each
//! composing the hub metadata ([`Hub`]) and carrying its own [`HubLifecycle`]
//! state. Authorities own exactly one domain, support registration with the
//! [`Registry`], expose no domain operations and contain no business logic.
//!
//! # Platform Kernel (Phase 7D.3)
//!
//! The **Platform Kernel** (the `kernel` module) is the live core of the
//! platform: the [`Kernel`] holds the built-in [`BuiltinAuthorities`] and
//! their [`Registry`], and the [`KernelInitializer`] owns the startup
//! orchestration — create, register, initialize, activate and verify
//! readiness (Platform Ready). It is startup orchestration only; no business
//! logic.
//!
//! # Lifecycle
//!
//! Every hub moves through the [`HubLifecycle`] states — `Registered`,
//! `Initialized`, `Active`, `Suspended` and `Shutdown`. Phase 7D.1 defines
//! the state **vocabulary**; Phase 7D.2 places the per-hub lifecycle state
//! on the concrete hub authorities (the `authority` module). Phase 7D.3
//! implements the **startup transitions** (`Registered → Initialized →
//! Active`); Phase 7F.5 completes the lifecycle with the **single validated
//! transition mechanism** ([`HubAuthority::transition`], backed by the one
//! transition table [`HubLifecycle::can_transition`]) and the
//! **`Suspended`/`Shutdown` transitions** (`Active ⇄ Suspended`, `Active |
//! Suspended → Shutdown`), driven in aggregate by the Platform Kernel (the
//! `kernel` module — `suspend`, `resume`, `shutdown`) so the eight
//! authorities transition together.
//!
//! # Routing
//!
//! The `routing` module defines the routing **contracts**: a [`HubRoute`] is
//! a source/target pair between two distinct hubs, expressed through the
//! Platform Backbone. The [`Router`] validates the routing contract, and the
//! Platform Backbone (the `backbone` module) is its first consumer — the
//! Phase 7E.1 runtime resolves targets and delivers through the routing
//! contract.
//!
//! # Platform Backbone (Phase 7E)
//!
//! The **Platform Backbone** is the communication infrastructure of the
//! platform — architecturally the Platform Backbone, implemented as the
//! Message Backbone. It is the single communication path (`Frontend →
//! PlatformInterface → Platform Backbone → Authority → Service → RA Core
//! Gateway (future) → RA Core`); no layer may bypass it. It transports
//! commands, requests, responses, events, notifications, lifecycle signals
//! and platform broadcasts.
//!
//! Phase 7E creates the **communication contracts only** (the `backbone`
//! module): the seven-kind message vocabulary
//! ([`backbone::BackboneMessageKind`]), the message envelope
//! ([`backbone::BackboneMessage`]) and the backbone interface
//! ([`backbone::Backbone`] — accept, route, dispatch, reply, broadcast). The
//! concrete [`backbone::PlatformBackbone`] is the **first consumer** of the
//! kernel's contracts — the [`Registry`], the [`HubGraph`], the [`Router`]
//! and the [`BuiltinAuthorities`] — and its attachment and operation are part
//! of kernel readiness. **Phase 7E.1** turns the contracts into the minimum
//! real backbone runtime: deterministic synchronous delivery to Active
//! authorities through the authority delivery boundary
//! ([`HubAuthority::receive`]) with [`backbone::DeliveryReceipt`] results.
//! Dispatch and delivery are real; services and payload processing are later
//! phases (TODO(Phase7F)).
//!
//! # Authority ownership
//!
//! The platform ownership chain is fixed: `Authority → State → Services →
//! Events → Policies`. An authority owns exactly one domain and owns that
//! domain's state, services, events and policies; **services never own
//! authorities**. The backbone dispatches to authorities — services are
//! reached through their owning authority, never directly.
//!
//! # Status
//!
//! Phase 7D.1: **contracts only**. Phase 7D.2: the concrete **hub
//! authorities** (the `authority` module) landed — one per initial domain,
//! composing the [`Hub`] metadata and carrying their [`HubLifecycle`] state.
//! Phase 7D.3: the **Platform Kernel** (the `kernel` module) brings the
//! authorities online — registration, startup lifecycle transitions
//! (`Registered → Initialized → Active`) and readiness verification
//! (Platform Ready). Phase 7D.3.1: **stabilization** — naming, visibility,
//! ownership and documentation synchronized ahead of the backbone. Phase 7E:
//! the **Platform Backbone** (the `backbone` module) lands the communication
//! contracts — vocabulary, envelope and interface — as the first consumer of
//! the registry, the graph, the routing contracts and the authorities, wired
//! into kernel readiness. Phase 7E.1: the **backbone runtime** — the minimum
//! real communication path (`accept → validate → resolve target → deliver →
//! return result`) with deterministic synchronous delivery, delivery receipts
//! and the authority delivery boundary ([`HubAuthority::receive`]) — without
//! touching the frozen kernel ownership. Phase 7F.1: the **service
//! architecture** — the common Service abstraction (the `service` module),
//! the [`service::ServiceResult`] vocabulary and the single Log proof
//! service owned by the Log Authority, reached through the authority
//! invocation boundary ([`HubAuthority::invoke`]). Phase 7F.2: the
//! **Platform Services** — the seven domain services (workspace, project,
//! package, settings, history, storage, device) bound to their authorities,
//! performing minimal deterministic domain operations and carrying the
//! minimal service-operation payload
//! ([`service::ServiceOperation`], [`BackbonePayload::Operation`]) — on top
//! of the frozen backbone and kernel. Phase 7F.3: **real per-domain
//! behavior** — the services own private domain state and perform real
//! domain operations (`Open`/`Close`, `Set`, `Record`/`Clear`, `Probe`), and
//! a `Request` carrying `Inspect` is answered with the synchronous
//! [`service::ServiceResult::Inspected`] Response; the payloads own their
//! arguments, so the message envelope is no longer `Copy`. Phase 7F.4: the
//! **Request → Response round-trip** — Requests carry an opaque
//! [`CorrelationId`] (minted by [`CorrelationSequence`]); the service result
//! is converted into an explicit [`Response`] message through the
//! [`ResponsePayload::from_service_result`](backbone::ResponsePayload::from_service_result)
//! boundary and delivered back over the backbone to the requesting caller;
//! the envelope gains the optional correlation field and
//! [`HubError::CorrelationMismatch`] guards the correlation. Phase 7F.5: the
//! **platform lifecycle & safe shutdown** — the lifecycle is completed with
//! the validated `Suspended`/`Shutdown` authority transitions
//! ([`HubLifecycle::can_transition`], [`HubAuthority::transition`]), the
//! kernel's aggregate suspend/resume/shutdown control, and the backbone's
//! per-authority `Active` gate rejecting all normal traffic while the
//! platform is suspended or shut down. Phase 7G.1: the **storage root +
//! save/load/recovery integration** — the platform storage root is resolved
//! and established at startup and threaded down the storage boundary to the
//! Storage Authority (`StorageService::with_root` →
//! `StorageAuthority::with_storage_root` →
//! `BuiltinAuthorities::with_storage_root` →
//! `KernelInitializer::initialize_with_storage`), and the Storage Service
//! performs the real `Save` / `Load` / `Recover` operations through the
//! existing Syss/Pss/Recovery stack. Phase 7H: **active objects** — the
//! `active_object` module lands the first genuine application-level objects
//! of the platform (Workspace, Project, Package, Document) with stable
//! strongly-typed identities and the validated `Closed ⇄ Open` lifecycle,
//! owned as domain state by the workspace/project/package services; the
//! workspace service performs the real document operations (open, close,
//! save, save_as, import, export) through the existing Syss/PSS stack.
//! Phase 7H.1: **workspace/project/package persistence** — the three
//! services persist their active objects through the same existing stack:
//! the object state (identity + recorded parent association) is serialized
//! with the `.ra` text codec and written atomically by Syss into the
//! existing `workspaces/`, `projects/` and `packages/` categories when the
//! object is opened; reopening restores state and association, closing and
//! shutdown preserve it, and corrupt or conflicting state is rejected
//! deterministically. Phase 7H.2: **platform-state domains** — the
//! Settings, History and Log services become real persisted platform-state
//! domains through the same existing stack (settings one file per key in
//! `settings/`, history as `history/history`, the smallest real structured
//! platform log as `logs/log`), lazy-loaded so corrupt state never fails
//! the boot; theme/view are settings-backed platform state with
//! deterministic defaults and validated values. Still missing: the device
//! connector and the RA Core Gateway.

// The module-wide dead-code allowances were removed in Phase 7E: the
// Platform Backbone (the `backbone` module) is the first consumer of the
// graph, the routing and the registry contracts, so the structural surface
// is live. A few accessors that only the tests and later phases use are
// still annotated individually, with the reason documented at each site.

mod active_object;
mod authority;
mod backbone;
mod graph;
mod kernel;
// The phase-specified layout is `hub/hub.rs`, so this submodule shares the
// parent module's name; `module_inception` is a false positive here.
#[allow(clippy::module_inception)]
mod hub;
mod hub_id;
mod lifecycle;
mod registry;
mod routing;
mod service;

use std::fmt;

    ActiveObjectId, ActiveObjectKind, Document, Package, Project, Workspace,
};
pub(crate) use authority::{
    DeviceAuthority, HistoryAuthority, HubAuthority, LogAuthority, PackageAuthority,
    ProjectAuthority, SettingsAuthority, StorageAuthority, WorkspaceAuthority,
};
pub(crate) use backbone::{
    Backbone, BackboneMessage, BackboneMessageKind, BackbonePayload, CorrelationId,
    CorrelationSequence, PlatformBackbone, Response, ResponsePayload,
};
pub(crate) use graph::HubGraph;
pub(crate) use hub::{Hub, HubDomain};
pub(crate) use hub_id::HubId;
pub(crate) use kernel::{BuiltinAuthorities, Kernel, KernelInitializer};
pub(crate) use lifecycle::HubLifecycle;
pub(crate) use registry::Registry;
pub(crate) use routing::Router;

// lib build reads them within the `service` module itself.

    LogRecord, LogSeverity, ServiceInvocation, ServiceOperation, ServiceResult,
};

/// Errors reported by the hub graph contracts.
///
/// The hub graph is internal to `ra-syss`; its errors are reported through
/// this type. As the Platform Backbone and Platform Services wire the graph
/// into the platform surface, these errors are converted into [`crate::Error`]
/// (via the `From<HubError>` bridge).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(crate) enum HubError {
    /// A hub with the same identifier is already registered.
    AlreadyRegistered(HubId),
    /// The hub is not registered and cannot be unregistered.
    NotRegistered(HubId),
    /// A route from a hub to itself was requested; a hub never routes to
    /// itself.
    SelfRoute(HubId),
    /// A lifecycle transition was requested from a state that does not allow
    /// it.
    InvalidTransition {
        /// The lifecycle state the hub was in.
        from: HubLifecycle,
        /// The lifecycle state the transition requested.
        to: HubLifecycle,
    },
    /// The platform kernel could not be verified ready.
    KernelNotReady,
    /// A backbone message references a hub that is not registered.
    UnregisteredTarget(HubId),
    /// A backbone message targets a hub that is not active (only active hubs
    /// are routed to).
    InactiveTarget(HubId),
    /// Routing and dispatch require a concrete target hub; broadcasts carry
    /// none.
    TargetRequired,
    /// A broadcast message carried a single target; broadcasts address the
    /// whole platform.
    TargetedBroadcast,
    /// A message kind does not fit the backbone operation it was offered to.
    ///
    /// E.g. a command (always targeted) offered to
    /// [`Backbone::broadcast`](backbone::Backbone::broadcast), or a
    /// non-response offered to [`Backbone::reply`](backbone::Backbone::reply).
    InvalidMessageKind {
        /// The kind of message that was offered.
        kind: backbone::BackboneMessageKind,
        /// The backbone operation the message was offered to.
        operation: &'static str,
    },
    /// The authority owns no ready service to invoke.
    ServiceUnavailable(HubId),
    /// A Response does not answer the Request it was expected to answer: its
    /// correlation identifier does not match (or is missing).
    CorrelationMismatch {
        /// The correlation identifier of the Request the Response should
        /// answer.
        expected: CorrelationId,
        /// The correlation identifier the Response actually carries, if any.
        actual: Option<CorrelationId>,
    },
}

impl fmt::Display for HubError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            HubError::AlreadyRegistered(id) => {
                write!(f, "hub {id} is already registered")
            }
            HubError::NotRegistered(id) => write!(f, "hub {id} is not registered"),
            HubError::SelfRoute(id) => write!(f, "hub {id} cannot route to itself"),
            HubError::InvalidTransition { from, to } => {
                write!(f, "hub cannot transition from {from} to {to}")
            }
            HubError::KernelNotReady => write!(f, "platform kernel is not ready"),
            HubError::UnregisteredTarget(id) => {
                write!(f, "message references unregistered hub {id}")
            }
            HubError::InactiveTarget(id) => {
                write!(f, "hub {id} is not active and cannot be dispatched to")
            }
            HubError::TargetRequired => write!(f, "routing requires a concrete target hub"),
            HubError::TargetedBroadcast => {
                write!(f, "broadcast messages carry no single target")
            }
            HubError::InvalidMessageKind { kind, operation } => {
                write!(f, "a {kind} message cannot be {operation}")
            }
            HubError::ServiceUnavailable(id) => {
                write!(f, "hub {id} has no ready service to invoke")
            }
            HubError::CorrelationMismatch { expected, actual } => match actual {
                Some(actual) => write!(
                    f,
                    "response correlation mismatch: expected request #{expected}, got request #{actual}"
                ),
                None => write!(
                    f,
                    "response correlation mismatch: expected request #{expected}, got none"
                ),
            },
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for HubError {}

/// Convenience alias for [`Result`](std::result::Result) fixed to [`HubError`].
pub(crate) type HubResult<T> = std::result::Result<T, HubError>;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn hub_errors_display() {
        let err = HubError::AlreadyRegistered(HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "hub workspace is already registered");
        let err = HubError::NotRegistered(HubId::LOG);
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "hub log is not registered");
        let err = HubError::SelfRoute(HubId::DEVICE);
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "hub device cannot route to itself");
        let err = HubError::InvalidTransition {
            from: HubLifecycle::Registered,
            to: HubLifecycle::Active,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "hub cannot transition from registered to active"
        );
        let err = HubError::KernelNotReady;
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "platform kernel is not ready");
        let err = HubError::UnregisteredTarget(HubId::LOG);
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "message references unregistered hub log");
        let err = HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::STORAGE);
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "hub storage is not active and cannot be dispatched to"
        );
        let err = HubError::TargetRequired;
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "routing requires a concrete target hub");
        let err = HubError::TargetedBroadcast;
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "broadcast messages carry no single target");
        let err = HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
            kind: backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            operation: "broadcast",
        };
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "a command message cannot be broadcast");
        let err = HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
            kind: backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            operation: "sent as a reply",
        };
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "a command message cannot be sent as a reply"
        );
        let err = HubError::ServiceUnavailable(HubId::LOG);
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "hub log has no ready service to invoke");
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let expected = sequence.next();
        let actual = sequence.next();
        let err = HubError::CorrelationMismatch {
            expected,
            actual: Some(actual),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "response correlation mismatch: expected request #1, got request #2"
        );
        let err = HubError::CorrelationMismatch {
            expected,
            actual: None,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "response correlation mismatch: expected request #1, got none"
        );
    }
}
